stem: A practitioner sees a patient on August 14 and considers issuing separate future Schedule II prescriptions. Which sets are consistent with the federal multiple-prescription framework, assuming legitimate medical purpose and state law are satisfied? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Two oxycodone prescriptions dated August 14 totaling 60 days, with the second carrying a lawful earliest-fill instruction
Three methylphenidate prescriptions postdated September, October, and November even though all were actually issued August 14
One oxycodone prescription written with five refills to create the same 90-day result
Three methylphenidate prescriptions all dated August 14, totaling 90 days, with appropriate earliest-fill instructions on the later prescriptions
Three lisdexamfetamine prescriptions all issued on August 14, totaling 90 days, with later prescriptions carrying earliest-fill dates

explanation.core_reasoning: Lawful future C-II therapy uses separate prescriptions issued on the real date with earliest-fill instructions; it does not use postdating or refills.

choice_analysis.A: Federal multiple-prescription structure is not limited to stimulants.
choice_analysis.B: Later prescriptions should not be postdated.
choice_analysis.D: That structure can fit the federal pathway.
choice_analysis.E: Separate C-II prescriptions may be staged this way.

related_facts: The federal total under this pathway may not exceed a 90-day supply.
explanation.mpje_trap: Thinking the rule applies only to ADHD stimulants or permits postdating.

reasoning_steps: Confirm each drug is Schedule II
Check issue date, total supply, and earliest-fill instructions
